sentences.text: No: for UCB personal loans, the directions say the bank may, at its option, provide a choice to switch to a fixed rate at the time of reset of interest rates, so the switch offer is permissive rather than mandatory.

The same directions also say that, when there is a reset of interest rates for an entire class of borrowers due to an increase in the reference benchmark, a UCB shall provide options including a switch to fixed interest rate only where such an option is provided by the bank.

The charge-disclosure rule applies if the bank provides the switch option, because applicable charges for switching from floating to fixed rate must be transparently disclosed in the sanction letter and when revised.
